summary: Nakalele Point Light on Maui's northwest point: established December 1908, automated October 1923, Coast Guard property; grounds open, tower closed.

structures.note: Fixed white lens-lantern light 20 feet above the ground on a platform on top of a small white house with red roof (Light-House Board notice, December 1908). Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends describe a light on a platform atop a keeper's house from 1910.

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett).

events.note: Rowlett: the original light on a mast was replaced by a light on a platform atop a keeper's house. Lighthouse Friends dates a keeper's dwelling and roof platform to 1910.
Changed to an automatic unattended light in October 1923 (Lighthouse Friends)
Changed to flashing white upon automation (Lighthouse Friends)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Society's place record gives latitude 21 02.89' and longitude 156 59.05' (roster.py matched it by name only, 41 km from the station record, and the station record's position agrees with the 1908 notice and the 2025 Light List). The 1908 notice gives 21 deg 2 min N, 156 deg 35 min 30 sec W, so the longitude on the Society's record is the error. The station record's coordinates are kept.

notes_for_editor: 1) Structure conflict left open: the December 1908 notice (Hawaiian Star, p. 2) describes a light on a platform atop a small white house, 20 ft above ground. Lighthouse Friends describes a 40-ft temporary mast and, by 1910, a keeper's dwelling with a roof platform; Rowlett says the mast light was replaced in 1910. The Society's 1924 comment (in the cached HTML only, not in the text the quote checker reads) describes an acetylene lantern on a small hut, then a metal pole; left out. 2) Hanuna's start date: Lighthouse Friends narrative 1910; its head-keeper list and the Society roster 1909. Both shown. 3) The USLHS place record has the wrong longitude (156 59.05'); roster.py matched it by name only (41 km from the station record). The roster lines are used because the name, island, 1908 date and keeper list match Lighthouse Friends. The place record's coordinates are not used. Confirm in a primary record before publication. Person slugs were checked against roster.py --json output on 2026-10-28. 4) The 1908 notice's position is OCR text: 'north 21 deg. 2 mln; longitude, west. 15c deg. 35 mln. 30 sec.' Read as 21 deg 2 min N, 156 deg 35 min 30 sec W: 'mln' is 'min'; '15c' is read as 156 because Lighthouse Friends gives -156.5899 and the 2025 Light List gives 156-35-25.742W. The story says 'about'. 5) Newspaper pages: the Hawaiian Star page (Dec 17 1908, sp=2) and the Pacific Commercial Advertiser page (June 21 1908, sp=3; the notice is dated June 20 and printed June 21) were read through the loc.gov cache. A 1919 to 1930 search for the 1923 automation notice found no hit. 6) The 2025 Light List, Volume VI, entry 28330 (Nakalele Point Light, Fl W 2.5s, range 6) is now footnoted as source 6 (npshistory copy of the same volume). 7) Keeper role 'Principal Lighthouse Keeper' is normalised to 'head keeper'. Other stations in the keepers' USLHS person records are not linked as other_stations. 8) Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett are treated as copyrighted: paraphrased, with one short quotation each. The rock-stack and coral description is from a note on the Lighthouse Friends page and is attributed to it. 9) NRHP status not checked (no NRHP number in the record). 10) No storms, wrecks or rescues were found in sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the 'a short walk' detail and the claim that both notices give only place and position were removed; the evidence for 'Rowlett lists it as active' now quotes the word 'Active'; the Light List facts are footnoted.
